question: Should completion delivery with incomplete observed account or thread metadata be treated as not visibly delivered for concrete requester routes, except for the proposed narrowly scoped non-threaded current-chat compatibility case?
rationale: This is an upgrade-sensitive user-visible delivery policy: strict matching avoids false success and misrouting, while accepting partial evidence preserves behavior for integrations that do not emit every route field. Source-level tests can prove either choice but cannot choose the durable product contract.

options.title: Adopt strict concrete-route evidence
options.body: Merge after documenting and testing that concrete requester account/thread routes require matching observed metadata, with only the current-chat exception retained.

options.title: Preserve broader partial-evidence compatibility
options.body: Revise the matcher so missing observed metadata may satisfy selected existing routes, with explicit tests defining the safe limits.

options.title: Pause for channel-owner review
options.body: Hold this PR until the affected channel owners confirm which outbound result shapes reliably include account and thread metadata.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict concrete-route evidence
recommendation.body: Merge after documenting and testing that concrete requester account/thread routes require matching observed metadata, with only the current-chat exception retained.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged route-isolation work is the closest established ownership signal for deciding how account-bound delivery-route invariants should apply.
